items.title: Public Meetings to Consider Zoning Amendments
RZ08/24 - 7120 Sixth Line, Belwood
notes: Mayor Watters indicated the public meeting is to present and receive public input regarding a proposed zoning by-law amendment on the subject land known as 7120 Sixth Line in the former Township of West Garafraxa.

He noted the purpose of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to change the zoning from “A - Agricultural” to “A - Agricultural Exception” on the retained parcel to restrict residential uses. The amendment also seeks to permit the maximum floor area for all accessory buildings to be 6.2% of the total lot area on the severed parcel.

The effect of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to implement zoning regulations necessary to facilitate a farm dwelling surplus severance and allow an increased maximum floor area on the severed parcel. The zoning amendment is a condition of approval of the County of Wellington Land Division Committee Application B54-24.

He indicated if a person or public body would otherwise have an ability to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) but the person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision.

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submission at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body may not be added as the party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters advised if anyone wishes to be notified of the adoption of the proposed zoning by-law amendment, a written request must be filed with the Municipal Clerk, Township of Centre Wellington, 1 MacDonald Square, Elora, ON, N0B 1S0.

The Municipal Clerk advised notice was mailed to prescribed persons, agencies and public bodies on or before January 23, 2025. A copy was also placed in the Wellington Advertiser on January 23, 2025. The Municipal Clerk confirmed the requirement for giving notice was completed on January 23, 2025.
Mayor Watters asked Deanna Maiden, Senior Development Planner, to introduce the application.

Deanna Maiden provided an overview of the application, indicating the purpose is to change the zoning to restrict residential uses on the retained parcel as well as permission for a maximum floor areas for all accessory buildings to be 6.2% of the total lot area on the severed parcel. She indicated the zoning bylaw amendment is to facilitate a farm dwelling surplus severance and allow an increased maximum floor area on the severed parcel.
Jeff Buisman, agent for the applicant, indicated he is available to respond to any questions.
Mayor Watters indicated there are no delegations registered and asked if there was anyone present who wished to speak to the application.

There being none, Mayor Watters asked for questions from Council There being no questions from Members of Council, Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and indicated Council will be considering the by-law at a future Council meeting.
He declared this public meeting adjourned.

items.title: Home Energy Efficiency Transition Program
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer indicated the Home Energy Efficiency Transition (HEET) program initiated by the County of Wellington plans to provide financial assistance to homeowners in Wellington County who wish o make energy-efficient upgrades to their homes. He introduced Karen Chisholme, Climate Change and Sustainability Manager, County of Wellington to outline the program.

Karen Chisholme indicated the purpose of the program is to accelerate the adoption of low-emissions and energy conservation home retrofits and address energy poverty. She outlined the program features, including financing and incentives, concierge, centralized web platform, climate-ready pathway plan and the promotion of low-carbon resilience and the terms of the loans. K. Chisholme noted the various roles and responsibilities of municipal staff and outlined the next steps in the process.
K. Chisholme responded to questions regarding incentives for multi- project initiatives, and coordination with other provincial and federal programs.

items.title: Ontario Heritage Act Alternative Notice Policy
notes: Report from M. Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services

Mariana Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services provided an overview of the report, indicating the Ontario Heritage Act requires notices to be published in a newspaper having general circulation in a municipality.

She explained the Ontario Heritage Act and the Municipal Act allow municipalities to adopt policies to publish notices in alternative media sources, such as a website. M. Iglesias indicated staff is recommending Council adopts the proposed draft Ontario Heritage Act Alternative Notice Policy allowing the Township to publish notices required by the Ontario Heritage Act on the Township’s website.

M. Iglesias responded to questions regarding the volume of notices currently placed in the newspaper, the estimated cost and time efficiency savings, no impact to right of appeal, and consolidation of notices.

items.title: Second Line Reconstruction Road Base Stabilization - BDT Product
notes: Procurement
Report from A. Gilmore, Manager of Engineering

Adam Gilmore, Manager of Engineering provided background on the collaboration with BDT and provided an overview of the Bioresin testing and the benefits. He outlined the proposed application of the BDT resin for the Second Line to strengthen the road base prior to repaving. A.

Gilmore noted the next steps to continue to monitor performance of the 2023 trial segment over time, the collection of more data from the larger scale application in 2024 and obtain Council’s endorsement of the 2025 application on the Second Line.
A. Gilmore responded to questions regarding the measurement of deflection, the benefits being less potholes, fewer repairs and longer life for the pavement.
